The finite $\wp$-slope condition means the $U_\wp$-eigenvalue of $\lambda$ is non-zero.  
By the old-form decomposition, any cusp form of level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$ with non-zero $U_\wp$-eigenvalue must lie in the old subspace coming from level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp)$, since $U_\wp$ acts nilpotently on the genuinely new quotient at level $\wp^r$.  

If $f$ is an eigenform at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp)$ with $U_\wp$-eigenvalue $\alpha\neq0$, then the forms $f\big|_k\!\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\wp^i\end{pmatrix}$ ($0\le i<r$) span the corresponding old subspace at level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$. On this space $U_\wp$ has characteristic polynomial $X^{r-1}(X-\alpha)$ (or $X^{r-2}(X^2-aX+b)$ if $f$ descends further to level prime to $\wp$); in either case the $\alpha$-eigenspace is one-dimensional.  

Hence each occurrence of $\lambda$ in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))$ gives exactly one occurrence in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$, and no new finite-slope occurrences arise. The multiplicities are equal, so the ratio is $1$.

\boxed{1}

The finite $\wp$-slope condition means that the eigenvalue of the Hecke operator $U_\wp$ attached to $\lambda$ is non-zero (hence of finite valuation).  

When one passes from level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp)$ to $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$, the space grows mainly by adding oldforms on which $U_\wp$ is nilpotent (infinite $\wp$-slope).  Localizing the Hecke algebra at the maximal ideal corresponding to $\lambda$, the control theorem for Drinfeld cuspforms of finite slope — or the direct oldform argument — shows that the $\lambda$-isotypic component does not enlarge: every $\wp$-finite-slope eigenform at level $\mathfrak n\wp^r$ already descends to level $\mathfrak n\wp$.  

Consequently the multiplicity of $\lambda$ in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$ equals its multiplicity in $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))$, so their ratio is $1$.

\boxed{1}

Let $a$ be the $U_\wp$-eigenvalue of $\lambda$; finite $\wp$-slope means $a\neq0$.  
The degeneracy maps $f\mapsto f(\wp^i z)$ ($0\le i<r$) embed $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))$ into $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$ as the old subspace. On the old subspace generated by a $\lambda$-eigenform, $U_\wp$ has characteristic polynomial $X^{\,r-1}\cdot P_{\lambda,\wp}(X)$, where $P_{\lambda,\wp}$ is the local Hecke polynomial at $\wp$ (degree $1$ or $2$ according to whether $\lambda$ already records $U_\wp$); thus each occurrence of $\lambda$ at level $\mathfrak n\wp$ contributes exactly once at level $\mathfrak n\wp^r$.

Any eigensystem new at level $\mathfrak n\wp^r$ with $r\ge2$ has $\wp^2$ dividing its level, and $U_\wp$ acts nilpotently on the new quotient (its $\wp$-slope is infinite). Hence no new finite-slope eigensystem can occur. Therefore
\[
\dim S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))[\lambda]
=
\dim S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))[\lambda],
\]
and the required ratio is $1$.

$$S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))\hookrightarrow S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$$
whose cokernel is killed by a power of $U_\wp$ (equivalently, $U_\wp$ acts nilpotently on the quotient). Hence the characteristic polynomial of $U_\wp$ on $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$ is the characteristic polynomial on $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))$ multiplied by a power of $X$. Only the infinite-slope (zero) eigenvalues acquire extra multiplicity, while every non-zero eigenvalue—i.e. every finite $\wp$-slope eigensystem—retains its original multiplicity. Therefore the ratio of multiplicities is $1$.
